tasks.title: Server-preference tie-break for every negotiator
tasks.goal: Add the `{ preferred }` option, which today only encodings take, to mediaTypes/mediaType, languages/language and charsets/charset, so a server can break a tie between values the client rates equally.
acceptance: With `Accept: text/html, application/json`, `mediaTypes(['text/html', 'application/json'], { preferred: ['application/json'] })` returns `['application/json', 'text/html']`, and `mediaType` with the same arguments returns `'application/json'`.
languages/language and charsets/charset take `{ preferred }` the same way: among equal q-values the preferred value comes first.
A lower q-value still loses: with `Accept-Language: en, fr;q=0.5`, `languages(['en', 'fr'], { preferred: ['fr'] })` keeps `en` first.
Calls without the option behave as before, and the existing tests still pass.
README.md documents the option for media types, languages and charsets, as it does for encodings.

hidden.reference: index.js passes options.preferred through; lib/mediaType.js, lib/language.js and lib/charset.js sort by q, then preference, then as before; README sections

tasks.title: Match HTTP response bodies
tasks.goal: Add an `expectBody` option (a substring, or a RegExp in the API) and a `--expect-body` CLI flag, so `http-get:` and `https-get:` resources count as available only once the response body contains the text.
acceptance: Against a local server, `expectBody` on an `http-get:` resource keeps waiting while the GET body does not contain the text, then succeeds once it does; a RegExp works the same way in the API.
It fails with the usual timeout error when the body never matches.
The options check rejects `expectBody` on a HEAD (`http:` or `https:`) resource straight away, with a clear message that names `expectBody` and the `-get` form to use instead.
The CLI takes `--expect-body <text>`, exits 0 once the body matches and non-zero on a timeout.
bin/usage.txt, README.md and index.d.ts document the option, the type tests cover it, and `npm test` (lint, types and mocha) passes.

hidden.reference: Joi schema entry, a HEAD check beside validateResources, a text response and a body match in the http check, the CLI flag, usage.txt, README, index.d.ts and test/types.test-d.ts

tasks.title: Format into, and parse from, a chosen unit
tasks.goal: Add a `unit` option: `format(value, { unit })` and `ms(number, { unit })` express the value in that unit, and `parse(str, { unit })` and `ms(string, { unit })` read a number without a unit in that unit. Keep the 100% coverage the repository enforces.
acceptance: `format(5400000, { unit: 'm' })` is `'90m'`, and with `{ unit: 'minutes', long: true }` it is `'90 minutes'`; the value is rounded to a whole number of that unit, as format() rounds today.
The unit takes any spelling and case the parser takes, such as `'m'`, `'Minutes'`, `'MINS'` or `'hrs'`, and the option is typed that way.
`parse('90', { unit: 's' })` is `90000`; a unit in the string wins, so `parse('2m', { unit: 's' })` is `120000`; without the option nothing changes.
An unknown unit throws an Error that names it, in format and in parse.
README.md documents the option, and both test runs (node and edge) pass with coverage still at 100%.

tasks.title: No Accept header means no media type
tasks.goal: When a request has no Accept header, `mediaType()` returns undefined and `mediaTypes()` returns an empty list, so a server can tell a client that asked for nothing from one that accepts anything.
acceptance: With no Accept header, `mediaType()` is `undefined` and `mediaTypes()` is `[]`.
With a list of available types and no Accept header, `mediaType(list)` still returns the first item.
The existing tests in test/mediaType.js stay exactly as they are.

hidden.why: test/mediaType.js asserts that no Accept header gives '*/*'; it is named in the acceptance, so the daemon locks it at the first assign. No change passes both, and editing it trips the tamper guard (verify.tamper: fail).
